runs.narrative: This commit does what its message describes: it removes the hardcoded dead Render.com address that was baked into the mobile app's authentication file and instead pulls the API address from the shared client configuration, so all four login-related network calls (send code, verify code, verify patient code, refresh session) now point at whatever address the demo startup script sets, which is the Cloudflare tunnel to the local backend. The diff matches the claim closely, changing exactly those four call sites and swapping the import as stated; I reviewed the code and message only and did not run the app. The one thing to note is that on-device verification is explicitly still outstanding: the accompanying status-doc update routes the work to a Device Tester step to run the demo and confirm OTP login actually reaches the backend, so this is code that looks complete and consistent but has not yet been tested. The commit is tied to story D1, which was attributed upstream, and the only other file touched is the routine project status document, which is expected housekeeping for this repo. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

The message also re-diagnoses an earlier note that had blamed ngrok for breaking encrypted connections: it says the real cause was ngrok's free-tier browser-warning page, worked around by sending an 'ngrok-skip-browser-warning' header on every request, and the commit's notes and the attached log show curl-based checks of the backend, the tunnel, and that header returning a healthy response. I have not run any of this; I am going only on the commit message, its diff, and the logs included. The commit explicitly frames its work as two parts in different states: the script switch, which it treats as finished and checked end-to-end, and a still-open part — adding the same header to the frontend API client (src/api/apiClient.ts), which is openly handed off to another agent, with an on-device re-test also still outstanding. Because one sub-item is explicitly unfinished, this is best tracked as Pending rather than complete. No story or issue was attributed to this commit, and none is needed here: it is a self-contained infrastructure change whose purpose is clear on its own. The files bundled in (script, status doc, and the two tracking logs) are the routine kind of companion updates this repository's commits normally carry, so there is no unrelated content to split out.

The code change matches what the message describes: the header is set once and applied to both network paths in that function, including the Expo Go fallback path, and the other changed files are just the routine project-state doc and the agent governance audit log, not unrelated material. The message claims the fix was checked with a curl test and a Node fetch smoke test with zero new TypeScript errors; I can't independently confirm those runs from the data given, but nothing in the diff contradicts them and the project-state notes corroborate the same account. The message is explicit that on-device testing through Expo Go has not happened yet and has been handed to a Device Tester, and since this is a transport-layer change that still needs that real-device check, it is best treated as code complete rather than tested. No story or issue was attributed to this commit upstream, and none is really needed here — it is a self-contained infrastructure fix whose purpose is clear from its own message and diff. Note that the PR this eventually merged under claims device verification was done, but that reflects the combined state of the whole PR at merge time, not this individual commit, which on its own is still awaiting that step. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

This commit builds out an "agent governance" system for the medrecord project: a set of hook scripts (under .claude/) that force a named agent to be declared before any file is edited, check which agent is allowed to touch which file, enforce a fix-and-retest loop when a testing agent reports defects, inject the current workflow state into a new session at startup, and write a trace-stamped audit log so a feature's full history can be reconstructed. It also registers all these hooks in the project settings and adds the supporting state files (agent registry, ownership registry, workflow state, and an event log). The code looks internally consistent with what the message describes, and no product story was attributed to it, which is fine here since this is a self-contained infrastructure and process change rather than feature work. The reason this is flagged: the commit deletes the file .claude/hooks/check-agent-declared.sh entirely, and the commit message never mentions removing it. It appears to be superseded by the new agent-gate.sh script, but since the message doesn't say so, this is a routine traceability gap worth a developer's quick confirmation. Separately, nothing in the message or diff shows that these hooks were actually run or tested, and the new code itself notes unverified behavior (the session-start hook's context injection has a known issue in some tool versions, and the subagent-stop hook won't fire in the project's current one-session-per-agent model), so this is not being marked as tested. The related pull request's claim of end-to-end device verification refers to the app and backend changes bundled alongside this work, not to these hook scripts.
